- **pdca-coder** — stack-agnostic executor for software tasks (code, tests, docs, refactoring, config).

- **pdca-collection** — a batch of tasks run as parallel PDCA lanes (worktree per group, `--no-ff` merge of completed groups).

Roles (planner, coder, check, scout, escalate) are bound by the host, so the

installation:
Copy the skills you want into an OpenCode skills directory.

Global (all projects):
```sh
git clone https://github.com/AlexeyShirshov/skills
cp -r skills/opencode/pdca skills/opencode/pdca-coder \
      skills/opencode/pdca-dotnet skills/opencode/pdca-collection \
      ~/.config/opencode/skills/
```

Per project:
```sh
mkdir -p .opencode/skills
cp -r skills/opencode/pdca* .opencode/skills/
```

Invoke a skill by name, for example `pdca-coder` for "by the cycle" code tasks.

installation:
## Prerequisites
- OpenCode 1.0.0 or later
- Node.js 18+
- git

## Installation

### Via curl (global)
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moah0911/aftermath/main/scripts/install.sh \
  | bash -s --
```

### Via npm
Add to your `opencode.json`:
```json
{ "plugin": ["@moah0911/aftermath"] }
```

### Project-only
```bash
git clone https://github.com/moah0911/aftermath
node aftermath/scripts/install.js --project
```

Restart OpenCode after installing (config loads at startup).

## Removal
```bash
node scripts/install.js --uninstall
```

BM25 over local files. No LLM, no embeddings, no network. Credentials are redacted at index time.
installation:

```json
  "plugin": ["opencode-deja"]
}
```

- 25 specialist agents (architect, planner, coder, reviewer, tester, debugger, risk-analyst, policy-enforcer, and more)
- 24 reusable workflow skills (TDD, security scan, deploy check, code review, and more)
- 17 workflow commands for all project operations
- 15 pre-built orchestration flows including Spec-Driven Development (SDD)
- Persistent state via `.planning/STATE.md` — resume exactly where you left off
- Wave-based parallel execution for independent tasks
- AI Safety layer: patch trust scoring, edit gates, phase gating, arch constraint enforcement, failure replay, and regression prediction
- Deep System Hooks: context monitoring, session idle summaries, shell environment injection
- Built-in MCPs: Context7 (docs), Exa (web search), Grep.app (code search)
- Ensemble Reasoning via `/fd-council` for synthesized consensus from multiple agents
- Persistent Memory with SQLite for tool executions and session summaries
installation:
### Method 1: curl (recommended)
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DVNghiem/flowdeck/main/install.sh | bash
```

### Method 2: npx
```bash
npx @dv.nghiem/flowdeck install
```

Core workflow commands:
- `/fd-new-project` — Bootstrap a new project with PROJECT.md, ROADMAP.md, STATE.md
- `/fd-discuss` — Pre-planning structured Q&A to capture decisions
- `/fd-plan` — Generate a wave-structured execution plan from decisions
- `/fd-new-feature` — Implement a feature with TDD discipline and parallel agents
- `/fd-checkpoint` — Save a session checkpoint to STATE.md
- `/fd-resume` — Reload STATE.md and PLAN.md to continue interrupted session

Thresholds are inherited by subagents by walking the parentID chain, `/autocompact off` reverts to normal behaviour, and with no threshold set the plugin has zero footprint. When a threshold applies, a chip joins the prompt footer and a side panel shows the numbers. Tested against 2.0.24.
installation:
## Install

```sh
opencode plugin add @hacky.software/opencode-autocompact
```

Or list it in `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["@hacky.software/opencode-autocompact"]
}
```

## Usage

```
/autocompact 500k      # compact this session (and its children) at 500k tokens
/autocompact 500000    # same, plain count
/autocompact 1m        # suffix form
/autocompact           # report the effective threshold and the model's limit
/autocompact off       # revert this session (and descendants) to normal auto-compaction
```

No configuration is required. The plugin does nothing until a threshold is set for a
session or one of its ancestors.

tagline: Peer discovery, messaging, and expiring file leases between concurrent OpenCode sessions
description:
Coordination for agents that share a workspace. Six tools let concurrent sessions
discover each other, talk to each other, and take exclusive expiring leases on the
files they are editing, so two agents never rewrite the same file at once.

- `crosstalk_status` / `crosstalk_peers` — declare a role, goal, and working set, then list who is running, what they declared, and what they hold
- `crosstalk_send` / `crosstalk_inbox` — message a session, a role, or everyone; mail lands in the recipient's mailbox and is injected into its current turn when the session is live
- `crosstalk_claim` — atomic lease on files or named resources; a refusal names the holder and when the lease expires
- `crosstalk_wait` — block until a peer goes idle or a resource is released, instead of sleeping and re-checking

Identity comes from the session rather than from tool input, so no session can
release another's lease or read another's mail. All six tools share one permission
action (`crosstalk`), so a project can allow or deny coordination with a single
rule. The core coordination logic (presence registry, mailboxes, claim table) is
host-free and unit tested — the plugin imports nothing from OpenCode outside its
single entry point.
installation:
## Prerequisites
- OpenCode 2.0.0 or later
- Node.js 22.18+ (OpenCode runs the TypeScript source directly, there is no build step)

## Install
```bash
git clone https://github.com/MrDoe/opencode-crosstalk
cd opencode-crosstalk && npm install
```

### Every project on this machine
```bash
npm run setup      # symlink this checkout into ~/.opencode/plugins/crosstalk
npm run uninstall  # remove the link again
```

The global `plugins/` directory is discovered automatically, so no config edit is
needed. Install into exactly one global root — linking both `~/.opencode/plugins/`
and `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` loads the plugin twice per location. Set
`CROSSTALK_PLUGINS_DIR` to target another directory.

### One project
Add to `opencode.jsonc`:
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["../opencode-crosstalk"]
}
```

Or symlink or copy the package into `.opencode/plugins/`, where it is discovered
with no configuration at all.

## Configuration
All options are optional and are set with the object form of `plugins`:
```json
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "../opencode-crosstalk",
      "options": {
        "scope": "project",
        "claimTtlMs": 300000,
        "codemode": false
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `namespace` | `crosstalk` | Tool namespace; dots are rejected. |
| `permission` | `crosstalk` | Permission action for all six tools. |
| `codemode` | `false` | Expose the tools through Code Mode instead of directly. |
| `scope` | `project` | Peer visibility: `project`, `location`, or `server`. |
| `claimTtlMs` | `300000` | Default lease duration. |
| `maxWaitMs` | `120000` | Ceiling on any blocking call. |
| `announce` | `true` | Add the coordination briefing to the system prompt. |

Bad values degrade to the default with a warning, so a typo never costs an agent
its tools mid-session. See the README for the full option table.

## Permissions
No rule is required to use the tools — OpenCode's base policy already allows the
`crosstalk` action. Add a rule to control it instead:
```json
{
  "permissions": [{ "action": "crosstalk", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" }]
}
```

## Removal
1. Run `npm run uninstall` in the checkout, or remove the symlinked directory
2. Remove the `plugins` entry from `opencode.jsonc` if you added one
3. `opencode service restart` if the plugin was already loaded in a running session

Any markdown file can be subscribed so its GFM checklists count as todos, and the TUI panel can tick them off by hand. Nudges are delivered as synthetic session input, so the model reads them as ordinary instructions. Tested against 2.0.24.
installation:
## Install

```sh
opencode plugin add @hacky.software/opencode-todo-supervisor
```

Or list it in `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["@hacky.software/opencode-todo-supervisor"]
}
```

## Configuration

Options are optional; the defaults supervise quietly in the background.

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "@hacky.software/opencode-todo-supervisor",
      "options": {
        "stallMinutes": 5,           // idle time before the first nudge
        "minNudgeIntervalMs": 45000, // rate limit between nudges
        "maxNoProgressNudges": 5,    // give up after this many no-progress nudges
        "injectTodoContext": true,   // remind the model of the list on each prompt
        "markdownFiles": ["PLAN.md"] // treat these files' checklists as the todo list
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Usage

Ask the agent to plan with `todo_write`, then check `todo_read`. In the TUI the composer
strip shows progress; open the panel from the command palette to add, remove or reorder
items, and to check off markdown checklist items.

- Source: https://github.com/veris-ai/veris-daytona/tree/main/daytona-opencode
- Docs: https://github.com/veris-ai/veris-daytona/tree/main/daytona-opencode#readme

## Installation

Add the plugin to `opencode.json`:

```jsonc
{ "plugin": ["@veris-ai/daytona-opencode"] }
```

Then export three keys:

```sh
export DAYTONA_API_KEY=...      # https://app.daytona.io/dashboard/keys
export VERIS_API_KEY=...        # https://studio.veris.ai
export VERIS_ENVIRONMENT_ID=... # the Veris environment that decides which vendor twins you get
```

Then run `opencode`. No image to build, no network configuration, nothing to start.

## What the agent gets

- The ten sandbox-backed tools from `@daytona/opencode`: bash, read, write, edit,
  multiedit, ls, glob, grep, getPreviewURL, gitSync.
- `verisReceipt`, which reports what the twin *received*.
- The Veris MCP server.

An empty receipt after a green run means the code never reached its dependency.
Ask an agent to call the Stripe API and it will report success whether or not it
made the call. The transcripts are identical; the receipts are not.

Eight sandbox-backed replacements for OpenCode's built-in tools (bash, read, write,

- `verisReceipt`: what the twin *received*, the tool that separates a real

  returning only once the changes are on your machine.
- `getPreviewURL`: the public URL for a port inside the sandbox.

An empty receipt after a green run means the code never reached its dependency.

## Links

- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@veris-ai/veris-sim-opencode
- Source: https://github.com/veris-ai/plugins/tree/main/veris-sim
- Docs: https://github.com/veris-ai/plugins#readme
- Veris: https://veris.ai

## Installation

```sh
opencode plugin @veris-ai/veris-sim-opencode -g
```

Equivalently, add `"@veris-ai/veris-sim-opencode"` to the `plugin` array in
`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. Then export your credential and restart
opencode:

```sh
export VERIS_API_KEY=...        # https://app.veris.ai
```

`VERIS_API_BASE` overrides the control plane (it defaults to
`https://svc.api.veris.ai`). Until the key is set, `opencode mcp list` shows the
`veris` server as failed; the commands still run, and `setup` walks you through it.

## Commands

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| `/veris-sim:setup` | wires the repository to a Veris environment, once: credential, environment, transport, one smoke run with proof of arrival |
| `/veris-sim:build <issue link \| prompt>` | measures every vendor claim the task rests on against the twin before designing, proves the change through veris-proxy with a receipt |
| `/veris-sim:fix <issue link \| prompt>` | reproduces the failure the issue describes before designing, proves the same failure closed with a receipt |

The three are plain OpenCode commands: only the engineer starts them, the model
cannot invoke them on its own. The same three are also registered as skills.

Tasks are non-blocking and cancellable (SIGTERM to the whole process group, then SIGKILL after a grace period), output is size-capped while streaming with truncation reported, and results carry real exit codes. Ships ~25 scripts (host health, disk, ports, docker ps/logs, git status, package updates), a wrapper that hands a whole task to a local CLI coding agent, and an MCP proxy that relays JSON-RPC to local stdio MCP servers. installation:
## Install the Duplex app
Download the installer for Windows / macOS / Linux from the
[Releases](https://github.com/Eric-huang799/duplex/releases) page (or build from source).

## Install the opencode mirror plugin
```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/plugins
curl -o ~/.config/opencode/plugins/cobrowse-mirror.ts \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eric-huang799/duplex/master/integrations/opencode/plugins/cobrowse-mirror.ts
```

## Register the MCP server
Add to `opencode.json` (project-level or global — see `opencode.example.json`):
```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "duplex": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["node", "/path/to/duplex/dist-bridge/index.cjs"],
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

Each one is independently probeable with `scripts/gate-probe.py`, which ships negative controls so a pass cannot be confused with a broken harness. installation:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/ebouther/opencode-unlimited-proxy && cd opencode-unlimited-proxy/stack
cp .env.example .env && sed -i 's/WARP_ACCEPT_TOS=0/WARP_ACCEPT_TOS=1/' .env
docker compose up -d --build
../scripts/smoke.sh
```

Then point any OpenAI-compatible client at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1`.

Only the gate probe is needed to *diagnose* the free tier, and it needs no
stack at all:

```bash
./scripts/gate-probe.py
```

tagline: Model-decided context handoff: close a milestone, write memory to disk, restart with a clean session
description: A relay-race alternative to compaction for long-running agents. Instead of a threshold rewriting the conversation in place, the agent itself decides when a milestone is closed, writes what the next session needs to disk, and hands over — the session ends and a fresh one picks up the baton. Memory lives in files (MEMORY.md overwritten, JOURNAL.md append-only, AGENTS.md for rules), so it is readable, diffable, correctable and survives the session. Four tools the agent calls itself: checkpoint (verifies by checksum that memory actually changed, rejects journal entries with no numbers in them, detects tampering with older entries), ask (pauses for a human decision, requires the agent to state what it would do without an answer), resume (refuses until the decision is written down), and loop (reopens the session and nothing else — it ends when the model declares --done or --blocked, not when a counter infers it). Measured on a local KAT-Coder V2.5 via llama.cpp: 7 milestones closed autonomously, 7 of 7 checkpoints invoked unprompted, 587 tests green, ~5,500 tokens of context per round instead of a compacted session restarting from 142,000 — and it does not grow across rounds. Pure bash, no dependencies; adapters/opencode/loop.sh is the opencode adapter and everything under core/ works with any agent that can run a shell command.
